subUnits.title: 1.1 Révision: Être, Avoir, et l'Accord des Adjectifs
notes: Révision: Être, Avoir, et l'Accord des Adjectifs
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to: consolidate mastery of être, avoir, and adjective agreement from previous terms.
Key Concepts:
1. Reviewing the Two Most Fundamental Irregular Verbs:
- ÊTRE (to be): je suis, tu es, il/elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont
- AVOIR (to have): j'ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont
- These two verbs appear in almost every French conversation and must be mastered AUTOMATICALLY.
2. Core Adjective Agreement Rule:
- Adjectives match the GENDER and NUMBER of the noun they describe.
- Masculine singular (base form) → +E feminine singular → +S masculine plural → +ES feminine plural

- KEY EXCEPTIONS: adjectives already ending in '-e' stay unchanged (honnête, timide, sympathique); some double a consonant (gentil→gentille, bon→bonne); some follow '-x'→'-se' (courageux→courageuse); beau/belle is fully irregular.
Formula Box:
être: je suis | tu es | il/elle est | nous sommes | vous êtes | ils/elles sont
avoir: j'ai | tu as | il/elle a | nous avons | vous avez | ils/elles ont
Agreement: base (m.sg) → +e (f.sg) → +s (m.pl) → +es (f.pl), with key exceptions
Analogy:

Reviewing être, avoir, and adjective agreement at the start of JSS3 is like a builder checking the FOUNDATION of a house before adding a new floor: no matter how exciting the new rooms (professions, health vocabulary) will be, they can only stand SOLID and SECURE if the foundation beneath them — the basic verbs and agreement rules — is genuinely strong first.
Common Mistakes to Avoid:
- Rushing into new JSS3 vocabulary without first confirming solid, automatic command of être, avoir, and agreement.
- Forgetting that some exceptions (like unchanging '-e' adjectives) are EXCEPTIONS to the general pattern, not the pattern itself.

quiz.q: What is the correct conjugation of 'être' for 'vous'?
quiz.explanation: 'Vous êtes' is the correct second-person plural/formal form of être.

quiz.q: What is the correct conjugation of 'avoir' for 'nous'?
quiz.explanation: 'Nous avons' is the correct first-person plural form of avoir.

quiz.q: What is the standard feminine singular adjective ending?
quiz.explanation: The standard feminine singular ending is +e added to the masculine base form.

quiz.q: What is the standard masculine plural adjective ending?
quiz.explanation: The standard masculine plural ending is +s added to the masculine base form.

quiz.q: Which of these adjectives is UNCHANGING in the feminine?
quiz.explanation: 'Honnête' already ends in '-e', so it stays unchanged in the feminine.

quiz.q: What is the feminine form of 'gentil'?
quiz.explanation: 'Gentil' doubles the final consonant and adds -e: gentille.

quiz.q: What is the feminine form of 'beau'?
quiz.explanation: 'Beau' is fully irregular in the feminine: belle.

quiz.q: How would you correct 'elle est intelligent'?
quiz.explanation: 'Elle' is feminine, so 'intelligent' needs feminine agreement: intelligente.

quiz.q: How would you correct 'il a les cheveux long'?
quiz.explanation: 'Les cheveux' is plural, so 'long' needs the plural form: longs.

quiz.q: Reviewing être, avoir, and agreement at the start of a new term is compared to ___.
opts: building a roof before any walls exist
a step with no real value
a builder checking a house's foundation before adding a new floor
quiz.explanation: Just as a builder checks the foundation before adding a new floor, a student must check these grammatical foundations before new material can build securely on them.

subUnits.title: 1.2 Révision: Aimer, Détester, et les Expressions Clés
notes: Révision: Aimer, Détester, et les Expressions Clés
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to: consolidate mastery of regular '-ER' verbs and key social expressions from JSS2.
Key Concepts:
1. The Regular '-ER' Verb Pattern — A Master Key:
- AIMER (to like): j'aime, tu aimes, il/elle aime, nous aimons, vous aimez, ils/elles aiment
- DÉTESTER (to hate): follows the IDENTICAL pattern as aimer.
- These verbs can be followed by an INFINITIVE (j'aime aller au cinéma) or a NOUN (je déteste l'orange).
- This SAME pattern applies to ADORER — a new verb introduced this term.
2. Key Social Expressions:
- merci (thank you), s'il vous plaît (please — formal), excusez-moi (excuse me)
- je crois que... / je pense que... (+que) — opinion followed by 'que'
- à mon avis... (in my opinion — NO 'que' follows!)
- TU (informal) vs. VOUS (formal/plural) distinction remains essential.
Formula Box:
aimer/détester pattern: -e | -es | -e | -ons | -ez | -ent
j'aime, tu aimes, il/elle aime, nous aimons, vous aimez, ils/elles aiment
je pense QUE... | je crois QUE... | à mon avis... (NO que)
Analogy:

The regular '-ER' verb pattern is like a MASTER KEY that opens MANY doors: once you have learned this ONE key thoroughly through aimer and détester, that SAME key will open the door to adorer this term, and to hundreds of other regular verbs in the years ahead.
Common Mistakes to Avoid:
- Forgetting that 'que' follows 'je crois' and 'je pense,' but NOT 'à mon avis.'
- Assuming a brand-new regular '-ER' verb (like adorer) needs entirely new memorisation — the SAME pattern from aimer/détester applies directly.

quiz.q: What is the correct conjugation of 'aimer' for 'elle'?
quiz.explanation: 'Elle aime' follows the regular -ER pattern: il/elle takes the base form + no ending change (-e).

quiz.q: What is the correct conjugation of 'aimer' for 'nous'?
quiz.explanation: 'Nous aimons' is the first-person plural form of the regular -ER verb aimer.

quiz.q: Which verb this term will follow the exact same pattern as aimer/détester?
quiz.explanation: 'Adorer' is a regular -ER verb and follows the identical conjugation pattern as aimer and détester.

quiz.q: What does 'merci' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Merci' means 'thank you' — an essential social expression.

quiz.q: What does 's'il vous plaît' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'S'il vous plaît' is the formal way to say 'please' in French.

quiz.q: Which opinion phrase is followed by 'que'?
opts: both, in exactly the same way
quiz.explanation: 'Je pense que...' and 'je crois que...' are followed by 'que'; 'à mon avis' is not.

quiz.q: Which opinion phrase stands alone, without 'que'?
quiz.explanation: 'À mon avis' (in my opinion) stands alone and is never followed by 'que.'

quiz.q: How would you say 'she likes going to the cinema'?
quiz.explanation: 'Elle aime' (correct conjugation) + infinitive 'aller' is the correct structure.

quiz.q: The regular '-ER' verb pattern is compared to ___ in this week's analogy.
opts: a key that opens only one single door
a key with no practical use
a master key that opens many doors
quiz.explanation: Learning one regular -ER pattern unlocks hundreds of other verbs, like a master key opening many doors.

quiz.q: Reviewing this toolkit at the start of the term prepares students for ___.
opts: this term's new content, which builds directly upon it
nothing relevant to the rest of the term
material that has no connection to prior learning
a completely unrelated set of topics
quiz.explanation: This term's new verbs (adorer, admirer, causer, affecter) all use this same -ER pattern, making the review directly useful.
